messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — p99 latency spike observed on streaming read path in us-west-2 (ingress -> decode). Automated SLO monitor tripped at 2023-07-11T15:10:56Z, severity: Sev2. Affected API: /v1/streams.generate. Initial p95: 220ms -> now 1.7s, p99: 720ms -> now 4.6s.

oncall-bot: Related signals: increased KV cache eviction rate, prefill hit-rate drop, elevated disk paging on cache-shard-7.

alex_k: I'm on it. seeing eviction-rate spike on shard-7 and slab churn in the prefill pool. Prefill vs decode allocation imbalance looks likely — prefill is flooding memory with large prefixes, decode workers are starving KV for contiguous slabs.

sarah_p: repro on dashboards: https://redwood-infra/dashboards/streams/latency?from=15m . Streaming stalls are correlated with prefill IO stalls.

alex_k: quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle prefill workers on shard-7 2) bump decode worker quota for shard-7 3) route new sessions away from us-west-2 to us-west-1 for non-urgent traffic.

devops_jc: Alexis, can you post the exact commands you want us to run? I can do a quick traffic shift.

alex_k: For throttling prefill: run on the prefill controller: 
```
kubectl -n inference exec prefill-controller-7 -- /bin/sh -c "svcctl set-rate prefill --shard 7 --qps 30"
```
Then on the decode pool: 
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/decode-pool-7 --replicas=8
```
Also enable immediate slab-rebalance: 
```
redis-cli -h shard-7.control CLUSTER REBALANCE-SLABS --target decode=60 --target prefill=20
```
(These are safe short-term ops, will monitor).

eva_r: I'll do the scale + rate change. Pushing now.

eva_r: done. prefill qps -> 30, decode replicas from 4 -> 8. Triggered slab rebalance command (patched to non-blocking).

alex_k: thanks. Observability: check this query for eviction-rate and prefill-vs-decode occupancy: 
```
avg_over_time(kv_evictions_total{shard=\"7\"}[5m])
avg_over_time(kv_prefill_occupancy{shard=\"7\"}[5m]) / avg_over_time(kv_decode_occupancy{shard=\"7\"}[5m])
```

sarah_p: after throttle + scale, eviction-rate down ~65% in 2m, prefill occupancy dropped ~40%, decode occupancy up ~25%. p95 dropped to ~350ms, p99 to ~980ms — still above SLO but trending.

cs-bot: Customer impact: several enterprise customers reporting timeouts for streaming sessions created between 15:04-15:12 UTC. CS flagged 3 high-priority tickets. Visible errors: 504 streaming timeout, partial chunks.

devops_jc: I'll start a controlled traffic shift: divert 20% of new sessions to us-west-1, 10% to us-east-1, keep existing sessions sticky. Rolling out now.

devops_jc: routing config pushed: 
```
routectl set-weight region=us-west-2 70 region=us-west-1 20 region=us-east-1 10 --for-route /v1/streams.generate
```

alex_k: Good. Also enabling short-term aggressive KV eviction backpressure to avoid disk paging: reduce cache soft_limit for shard-7 by 30%. That should lower page-ins.

alex_k: command: 
```
cachectl set soft_limit --shard 7 --percent 70
```

eva_r: doing that now.

eva_r: soft limit set. disk IO dropped, iostat shows reduction in r/s on cache-7.

sarah_p: metrics update: 3m after all changes p95=180ms, p99=420ms, streaming stalls mostly cleared. No further increase in eviction rate.

alex_k: planning follow-ups: - run background slab-defrag on shard-7 during low-traffic window - add guardrails to prefill to respect decode occupancy ratios - add alert for prefill:decode occupancy delta > 2.0 - postmortem to owner the root cause (weakened prefill throttling after last deploy?)

devops_jc: I'll schedule slab-defrag at 02:00 UTC with a rolling window and <5% traffic drain.

cs-bot: Notifying affected customers and updating tickets with mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution. Assigned CS rep: @michael_c.

alex_k: Handoff — @sarah_p taking next watch for regression. If p99 creeps >700ms, escalate to infra-sev1 and re-enable emergency reroute to standby region (50% traffic).

sarah_p: taking watch. I'll post updates every 10m for the next hour and run the defrag runbook once slab-stability holds.

cs-bot: All customers with active streaming sessions during the window have been notified. SLO impact estimated: 0.4% uptime loss for streams.generate for the 8-minute window.

alex_k: root cause hypothesis for postmortem: prefill allocation policy did not cap memory per-shard under certain request mixes (long-prefix customers + bursty prefill), causing fragmentation -> forced evictions -> disk paging -> tail latency.

sarah_p: adding links to logs and graphs: https://redwood-logs/streams/shard-7/?from=2023-07-11T15:00Z&to=2023-07-11T15:30Z

alex_k: thanks team. Closing thread for now, leaving watch to @sarah_p. If anything regresses, ping here and I'll rejoin. :thumbsup:
